name: Question 5
problem:
The third-order differential equation 

$$
{y}^{‴}-{y}^{″}+3{y}^{′}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,y=2t
$$

can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}={x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}^{′}=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{1}(t)=y(t),$ ${x}_{2}(t)={y}^{′}(t)$ and ${x}_{3}(t)={y}^{″}(t).$ Find the function $f(t).$
worked_solution:
First, we make the following change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =y \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={y}^{′} \\ {x}_{3}(t) & ={y}^{″}\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the above equations with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) & ={y}^{′} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t) & ={y}^{″} \\ {x}_{3}^{′}(t) & ={y}^{‴}\end{aligned}
$$

which we can rewrite as 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2}, \\ {x}_{2}^{′}={x}_{3}, \\ {x}_{3}^{′}={y}^{‴}.\end{aligned}
$$

At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of ${x}_{1},$ ${x}_{2},$ and ${x}_{3}.$

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative $({y}^{‴}),$ we obtain

$$
{y}^{‴}={y}^{″}-3{y}^{′}+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,y+2t.
$$

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives

$$
{y}^{‴}={x}_{3}-3{x}_{2}+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{x}_{1}+2t.
$$

Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side. 

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2}, \\ {x}_{2}^{′}={x}_{3}, \\ {x}_{3}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}+2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
f(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}+2t.
$$

Question 5
?

The third-order differential equation y‴−y″+3y′−cos⁡ty=2t can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows: {x1′=x2x2′=x3x3′=f(t) where x1(t)=y(t), x2(t)=y′(t) and x3(t)=y″(t). Find the function f(t).

a
−cos⁡tx1+3x2−x3−2t
b
3x1−cos⁡t+x3+2t
c
x1−3x2+cos⁡tx3+2t
d
cos⁡tx1−3x2+x3+2t
e
−x1+3x2−cos⁡tx3−2t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we make the following change of variables: x1(t)=yx2(t)=y′x3(t)=y″

Differentiating the above equations with respect to t, we get x1′(t)=y′x2′(t)=y″x3′(t)=y‴

which we can rewrite as {x1′=x2,x2′=x3,x3′=y‴.

At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of x1, x2, and x3.

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative (y‴), we obtain y‴=y″−3y′+cos⁡ty+2t.

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives y‴=x3−3x2+cos⁡tx1+2t.

Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows: {x1′=x2,x2′=x3,x3′=cos⁡tx1−3x2+x3+2t.

Finally, f(t)=cos⁡tx1−3x2+x3+2t.
